newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART CRASH AT ST PAULI, FAIL TO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART CRASH AT ST PAULI, FAIL TO GO TOP.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart missed out on their the chance to overtake Bayern Munich at the top of the German first division on Saturday by unexpectedly crashing 2-1 at lowly St Pauli.

Midfielder Christian Springer bagged both goals for the unfashionable Hamburg side while Stuttgart's feared striking force made most of the play but managed only a penalty, converted by Bulgaria's Krasimir Balakov.
The defeat left the 1992 champions in second place on 27 points from 13 matches, one point behind Bayern, who drew 1-1 with local rivals 1860 Munich on Friday.
Springer scored St Pauli's first from a free kick in the 12th minute then added another on the break in the 71st as Stuttgart were themselves driving forward in search of the winner.
"It was a bitter defeat all right," said Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew. "A win would have put daylight between us and Bayern."
As Stuttgart faltered, the pack took the opportunity to close the gap behind them.
Early season leaders Bayer Leverkusen joined them on 27 points with a 3-0 defeat of hapless Borussia Moenchengladbach, who were welcoming back Sweden's Martin Dahlin from Roma.
Leverkusen scored three times in the second half despite being reduced to 10 men as early as the 25th minute when libero Jens Nowotny was sent off for a second bookable offence.
"We needed to win not to lose touch with the leaders," said coach Christoph Daum. "If anything, going down to 10 men was just the spur we needed."
The defeat meant Moenchengladbach have now gone over 11 hours without scoring an away goal in the Bundesliga.

Champions Borussia Dortmund, 2-1 losers at home to Atletico Madrid in the European Champions' League on Wednesday, bounced back with a 3-1 victory at Schalke before 71,000 fans in the Ruhr district derby in Gelsenkirchen.

Heiko Herrlich put Dortmund ahead in the 15th minute but it was Swiss international Stephane Chapuisat who turned his injury-depleted side's dominance into goals in the 62nd and 64th minutes, all within 10 minutes of coming on as substitute.
Martin Max had equalised for Schalke in the 58th minute.
The day's other surprise result came at Duisburg where fellow strugglers Freiburg won 4-1 thanks to a hat-trick from Uwe Wassmer.
